ancestry.discovery.total_individuals.method: sum of NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS over initial-stage ancestry rows. The total is a sum of study sample sizes, not a count of distinct people. Asthma GWAS draw repeatedly on the same large cohorts, so a participant enrolled in several studies is counted once per study, and studies mapped to asthma alongside another trait contribute their whole sample. The total is therefore much larger than the number of people who have ever been in an asthma GWAS, and must never be reported as a headcount. What the shares describe is how the field's accumulated asthma evidence is distributed across ancestry groups, which is the question this module asks. A row naming one broad ancestral category contributes all its individuals to that category; a row naming k categories contributes an equal 1/k share to each. The catalog publishes no per-category count within a row, so the equal split is an assumption. It preserves the total, so the shares describe one denominator.

ancestry.loci.17q12-21.associations.method: genome-wide-significant asthma associations mapped to 17q12-21 (ORMDL3/GSDMB). An association is assigned to a locus when any symbol in the GWAS Catalog's own MAPPED_GENE cell for that association equals one of the locus's gene_symbols, compared case-sensitively after splitting the cell on its separators and trimming. MAPPED_GENE is the catalog's gene annotation, so the match is against a curated identifier and never against free text in a trait or study title. REPORTED GENE(S) is deliberately not used: it carries the authors' own wording, which is not a controlled field. No genomic window is applied, because a window needs a genome build the extract does not state per row.
